authority: Defra Data Services Platform and data.gov.uk

claims.statement: The official 1m Composite DTM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The DTM removes surface objects from the DSM using algorithms and manual editing to represent the terrain surface.
The 2022 composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest best-resolution data is used.
Bilinear interpolation is used where source data is resampled before merging.
The documented 2022 composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 through 2 April 2022.
The metadata-index catalogues identify which survey contributed at a location.
Composite DTM data is delivered as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevations are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15 for the composite.
Input LIDAR surveys are documented with plus or minus 15cm RMSE vertical accuracy.
Time Stamped DTM archive data can be available at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m resolution depending on the survey.
The transformation and geoidal model for Time Stamped data depend on survey period and must be read from metadata.
DTM represents bare terrain while DSM includes vehicles, buildings, vegetation and other surface objects.
The Data Services Platform documents a WCS endpoint for the 1m Composite DTM.
No exact TQ2892 filtered feature response, coverage bytes, raster cell lineage or numeric candidate elevations were captured.
